instructions: Finely chop the onion and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Pull the 12 oz Oaxaca cheese apart into thin strings. If yours is a block, shred it on the big holes of a box grater instead.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 10 inch oven-safe skillet over medium. Squeeze the 6 oz chorizo out of its casing into the pan.
Cook the chorizo for about 6 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until it's crumbly and browned all over.
Tilt the pan and spoon off most of the fat, leaving about a tablespoon behind.
Add the onion and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft.
Add the garlic and the can of green chiles and stir for 1 minute, until you can smell the garlic.
Spread the chorizo mixture evenly over the bottom of the pan and scatter the cheese over the top.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted and is bubbling at the edges. Take it out as soon as it's melted. Any longer and the cheese turns firm.
Meanwhile, chop a small handful of the cilantro.
Use an oven mitt to set the skillet on a trivet. The handle is very hot. Scatter the cilantro over the cheese.
Serve right away, straight from the skillet, with the tortilla chips.
method_notes: Both versions brown fresh Mexican chorizo in an oven-safe skillet, drain off the fat, soften onion and garlic, spread it in the pan under a layer of melting cheese and bake at 350°F only until the cheese is gooey. The Daring Gourmet adds canned roasted green chiles (or roasted poblanos), uses a pound of cheese for six and warns that overbaking makes the cheese firm. Tara's Multicultural Table uses Oaxaca or Monterey Jack for four, saves a little chorizo to scatter on top and serves it with roasted salsa and tortillas or chips. This one follows The Daring Gourmet's method, sized to 12 oz of cheese.
